description: The Alibaba Cluster Trace Program publishes traces from Alibaba's production data centres to help researchers understand modern clusters and test scheduling and resource-management ideas with realistic data. Releases include cluster-trace-v2017 (about 1,300 machines over 12 hours, co-located online services and batch jobs), v2018 (about 4,000 machines over 8 days with batch job DAGs), GPU traces from 2020 (over 6,500 GPUs over two months of machine-learning workloads), 2023 and 2025, a 2021 microservices trace with call dependencies and response times for over 20,000 microservices, a 2022 microarchitecture trace, and 2026 releases on a six-month GPU cluster of up to 155,410 GPUs, generative-AI serving and LLM inference. Alibaba publishes them with documentation, schemas and lists of papers that used them. Coverage: Alibaba data centres in China (not individually identified), from hours to six months per trace, at second to minute resolution. Format and access: CSV and similar files downloaded from links in the GitHub repository; free of charge for research, with users asked to cite the related papers; the README states no formal licence. Caveats: anonymised and normalised values; each trace has its own schema and period; no facility-level power or cooling data. Simulation uses: demand and operation inputs and synthetic benchmarks for data-centre scheduling, capacity planning and optimisation, and studies of AI workload growth. Related records: Google cluster workload traces and the Azure Public Dataset are comparable, and CloudSim, CloudSim Plus and SimGrid can replay such workloads.
